# One instance built at run time writes page state another reads, on every
# target.
#
# A write splices an update after it for every node, slot and instance that
# reads what it wrote, whatever body they are in -- right where the bodies
# are spliced into one, and wrong where an instance is a record of its own:
# `chooser`'s click named `shower`'s `#shown` through chooser's record,
# which has no such field, and fyne and gtk4 did not build. A write from a
# component's body now updates only what that body and the page hold. The
# other instance reads the state where it is built, so `shower`, built after
# the write, shows it.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import test "sngl:test"

var picked = "a"

component chooser ui.node {
    var count = 0

    ui.button #pick(text="pick b", @click {
        count += 1
        picked = "b"
    })
}

component shower ui.node {
    var seen = 0

    ui.text #shown(value="picked {picked}")
}

component main ui.node {
    var away = false

    ui.button #leave(text="leave", @click { away = !away })
    if away {
        shower #s
    } else {
        chooser #c
    }
}

func testTheOtherInstanceReadsTheWrite(t test.Test, c main) {
    if c.c != null {
        c.c.pick.click()
    }
    t.assert(picked == "b")
    c.leave.click()
    t.assert(c.s != null && c.s.shown.value == "picked b")
}
